name: Workout of the day from your training sheet (Zvid)

parameters.content:
## Workout of the day, on autopilot

Every morning at 06:00 this workflow reads today's row from your training
sheet and renders a 1080x1920 workout-of-the-day video: hero-footage hook,
the full board (up to five exercises with reps) and the coach's note —
ready for Stories, Reels, Shorts or the gym's group chat.

### Setup (about three minutes)

**The first run renders for real and spends credits** (~13, see Cost below).
Want a free preview instead? Set `dryRun: true` in `Config` before step 4.

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach a Google Sheets credential to *Read workout
   sheet* and pick your spreadsheet + sheet. Columns are on the sheet note.
3. **Open `Config`** and set `gymName`, `handle` and your `accent` colour.
   Swap `heroVideo` for your own gym footage (any public MP4 URL) when you
   have some — portrait clips look best on the 1080x1920 canvas.
4. Run **Test manually**. *Validate project (free)* runs first and quotes the
   exact cost, then the render starts automatically — so this run spends
   about 13 credits. When it finishes, click **▶ Watch video** to play the
   result inside n8n.
   With `dryRun: true` it stops after validation instead: a free draft plus
   an **editorLink** into the Zvid editor, and nothing is charged.
5. **Activate the workflow** for the daily 06:00 schedule.

### Cost per video

A ~13 second 1080x1920 render is **about 13 Zvid credits**. *Validate project
(free)* still returns that exact number before every render — it is just no
longer a stopping point. Free accounts include enough credits to test.

## Your training sheet

One row per day, header row required:

| Column | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Date | `2026-07-27` — YYYY-MM-DD, format the column as plain text |
| WorkoutName | `PUSH DAY 01` |
| Focus | `Chest / Shoulders / Triceps` |
| Ex1 … Ex5 | `Bench press x 5x5` — "Exercise x Reps", reps come after the **last** " x " |
| CoachNote | `Rest 90s between sets.` |

- Blank Ex cells are skipped; at least **Ex1** is required.
- An Ex cell without " x " renders without a reps line — `400m run` works.
- No row for today? The run stops with a clear error. Prefer reusing the
  most recent past workout instead? Set `fallbackToLatest: true` in Config —
  the video always shows that row's own date, never a wrong one.
- Dates are matched in your n8n instance's timezone; set `timezone` in
  Config (e.g. `America/New_York`) if your gym lives elsewhere.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap them for native nodes:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

The Zvid Trigger removes the polling loop entirely.

## Dry run — the free opt-in

`dryRun` is `false` by default, so a run goes straight down the render
branch and spends credits (~13 per video).

Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** and the workflow stops here instead: the
project is validated, saved as a **draft**, and reported with an
**editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the video back, adjust anything by hand, and see the exact
credit cost — without spending a single credit. Saving a draft is free.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` (the default) when you want the render.

## Posting it somewhere

**Run summary** carries `videoUrl` plus a ready-to-paste `caption` built from
your sheet row (workout, focus, every exercise with reps, the coach's note
and hashtags). **▶ Watch video** after it carries the MP4 itself as binary
`data`.

Attach any platform node after **▶ Watch video** — the file is already on the
item, and the text is one expression away:
`{{ $('Run summary').first().json.caption }}`

- **Instagram / Facebook Reels** — Facebook Graph API node
- **TikTok / YouTube Shorts** — their upload nodes, or an HTTP Request
- **Google Drive / Slack / Email** — drop the file wherever the team lives

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button — today's workout, no URL to copy.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (plus `caption`, `jobId`
and `creditsCharged`) if you want to pipe the result onward.
